claims.claim: IREN's FY26 10-K reports a geographically diversified announced data-center pipeline across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific, including 750MW at Childress, 2GW across Sweetwater 1-2, 1.6GW at Kiowa, 800MW at Bundey and 300MW at Badajoz.

IREN disclosed a multi-generation compute portfolio including NVIDIA H100/H200/B200/B300/GB300/VR200 and AMD MI350X systems, plus supplier relationships spanning NVIDIA, AMD, Dell, Lenovo, Supermicro and Gigabyte.

The FY26 10-K states Horizon 1 was accepted by Microsoft in August 2026, while Horizon 2-4 are targeted for phased delivery in Q4 2026 with contractual grace periods extending as late as early Q2 2027.
IREN completed the Mirantis acquisition in August 2026 for approximately $544 million, adding cloud orchestration, monitoring and enterprise-support capabilities and roughly 580 personnel.

factors.name: crossDivisionLeverage
factors.basis: The Mirantis acquisition adds orchestration, monitoring, lifecycle management and enterprise support on top of IREN's power, data-center and compute layers, creating a more integrated infrastructure stack.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: IREN has relationships across multiple GPU/OEM vendors and multiple GPU generations, but the 10-K explicitly says GPU/networking demand exceeds supply and certain AI hardware comes from a limited supplier set.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Geographic pipeline diversification and multi-vendor compute broaden deployment options, while delivery still depends on power, construction, hardware availability and substantial financing.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: The disclosed multi-gigawatt site pipeline plus integrated compute/software stack gives IREN control over scarce power-to-compute conversion capacity, though execution remains required before planned MW become productive capacity.

risks.risk: The 10-K states demand for NVIDIA GPUs and certain networking equipment exceeds supply and that IREN sources important AI hardware from a limited number of suppliers, creating delivery and cost sensitivity.
IREN expects substantial additional capital requirements and may commit to GPU purchases or site development before related financing or customer contracts are complete.
Microsoft Horizon 2-4 delivery grace periods extending into early Q2 2027 mean Q4 2026 target dates should not be treated as hard realized-revenue dates.

unknowns.unknown: The filing establishes supplier relationships and pipeline capacity but does not establish that all planned MW are financed, energized or contracted; Alpha should distinguish planned capacity from productive capacity.

claims.claim: Horizon 1 was accepted by Microsoft in August 2026; Horizon 2-4 remain targeted for phased Q4 2026 delivery, with contractual grace periods extending from mid-Q4 2026 through early Q2 2027.

The Microsoft agreement has approximately $9.7 billion total contract value through 2031 and uses 20% prepayments per tranche, while acceptance of each tranche affects associated guarantee release mechanics.

factors.name: expectationsExecution
factors.basis: Horizon 1 acceptance is concrete execution evidence, but remaining tranches retain delivery windows and grace periods, so future contract conversion is not yet realized.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: The filing establishes large contract value and prepayment structure but does not provide enough comparable unit economics to infer durable pricing power without Alpha's calibration.

risks.risk: If a funded Microsoft tranche is validly terminated and a qualified replacement customer is not secured during the remarketing period, parent guarantees can expose IREN to allocated debt/note and termination-related obligations described in the filing.

unknowns.unknown: Realized margins and customer acceptance timing for Horizon 2-4 remain unobserved; contract value and target delivery should not be substituted for GAAP revenue or profitability.
